questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a destination where the main language was english, and having been to Australia once before and falling in love with the country, i wanted to revisit, but go to a spot i had never been. At first i considered studying in Brisbane itself, but luckily, i chose to study at Griffith University Gold Coast Campus, which is the best decision i have made in a long time. I wanted to be close to nature, and close to the sea, to really experience the aussie surf culture, and one can definitely say i got to do that, as i ended up living 100 meters from the beach with a balcony view. I also prioritized that the university had subjects that would fit into my degree, as i have mandatory courses that needed to be heeded, but other than that, they offered a great array of electives. The australian structuring of years and classes permittet that i took whatever classes made sense in terms of KU, and in terms of scheduling, as long as i could live up to the prereqs put in place.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got truly immersed in my experience, as i chose to seek out other internationals and australians. I definitely got out of my comfort zone and tried new things, went on roadtrips, learned to surf, caught the sunrises and built up  network of international and australian friends i will have for life. Studying in Australia was surprisingly tough. It seems that psychology is one of the only majors i encountered in Oz that we at home describe as social science, but in Australia, it is mostly natural sciences. this meant way more lab reports, statistics, academical writing and literature searches than i had anticipated. I ended up collectively in 4 courses writing 5 different six-page reports of my own academic research on a given topic, and in one case also conducting a study on myself for 5 weeks in advance. furthermore, a lot of very specific knowledge was required for exams, and i spend a lot of time memorizing stuff in order to pass exams.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: very easy! the student help centre and the student guild were amazingly helpful and provided all the ressources needed for university, alas, you had to seek them out, if you didnt participate in the orientation week, which i HIGHLY recommend you do! showing up to the first activity "Mates in minutes" led me to meet the people i would spend the rest of the semester with, go on trips with, and later travel with. go to orientation week please! I definitely, unfortunately, noticed that the people who didnt go had a harder time making friends, as people all have different majors and different classes

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: orientation week had stalls and tours, where we got to talk to the different couselling offices, learn where all the important things were, and were handed a "manual" to what was going on on campus, outside campus in gold coast etc. I didnt need any help with scheduling or something of that sort, and i didnt live on campus (please dont if possible, its much better and cheaper to live elsewhere, closer to the beach and facilities, and you can still make friends living outside the campus village). If you lived on campus, they had a bunch of introductory events, and also welcoming officers to sho you around the campus village.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
it was really nice - the Griffith mates were SO eager to help, and stuck around all semester, making fun activities and providing opportunities to meet new people. Just go to as many events as possible - they may sometimes seem lame, but i promise, its worth it! 
The mates events and orientation week stuff is both on and off campus, giving you a chance to see the city of Gold Coast as well (Which is quite big for a small town).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started searching for housing on Flatmates finders about 3 weeks before leaving for australia. Its easy to find housing if you do it before the semester starts, but really hard once the semester has started. it felt daunting having to transfer deposit and rent to someone unknown, but flatmates is the safest way, unless you know someone who is renting out, to find a flatmate

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
and you gotta be careful - i know more than one person who showed up and had been scammed! be really allert to who the person is youre dealing with, see if you can find the house on maps, find the person on social media etc etc. I ended up paying 350$ AUD a week, about 6300 kroner a month - and thats very cheap for the surfers paradise location i ended up living in at Cavill Avenue. in general, try to see if you can live somewhere along the tram-line. The busses are really bad in gold coast, and it is NOT cycleable. like, i thought "bah! i can bike anywhere!" but no - there is no way. The trip from surfers paradise to uni is 30 minutes in tram, 5 km by car or 10 km by bike because of the roads?! not ideal.
if you live on campus, grocery stores are hard to get to, and its quite far away from the beach, nightlife and culture - i would definitely go for living in surfers, or if you can handle the 45 minutes by tram (the tram is nice though), definitely do mermaid waters or burleigh, if you plan to have a car. in general as a rule, Gold coast gets nicer, the closer you get to the NSW border haha

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
the housing market is in crisis, and the specific student housing is a joke - the on campus living was 5 room shared apartment with 2 shared bathrooms and a shared kitchen. th kitchen doesnt have an oven, no microwave, no kettle, no pans, only a stovetop and a medium sized fridge that people have to share. 
all in all- find your own room, youre better off that way. but if you do, please show up to O-week - its worth it!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the course registration was easy as, when first i had my clearance from KU to actualy take the courses. remember to upload your transcript from high school in ENGLISH - that caused me a bit of trouble.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you get your griffith login, and then from the beginning of may, you can start registering for the courses you wish to take. be mindful of which campus they are offered at. mount gravatt, nathan, logan and brisbane are quite far from the gold coast campus. if the courses werent working out, you could just go down to the student help centre and get them changed around . i didnt

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: student help centre was there everyday and seemed very helpful and friendly. much more responsive and available than student counselling at KU

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got all the classes i wanted - had to fight a little for my right to take a cognition neuro psych course and the cognition psych course that was its prereq at the same time, but the administration at griffith understood why i took both at once and gave me dispensation.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure you have a lot of options, in regards to choosing your courses - griffith has 3 trimesters, and some courses only run one of them. i didnt take workplace psych, because all the good workplace psych courses were in trimester 1, and i was there in tri 2.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was really hard work, and quite a lot repetition, memorization, and there were definitely too much online coursework. i drowned in stuff to do, because i had 2 hour lectures 6 times in the semester in 3 of my courses, 2 hour tutorials each week in all courses but one, and also had 2-4 hours of online learning (mostly repetition but also sprinkled with new necessary stuff) every week. online session would take at least double the allocated time to go through. there were a lot of assignments, and it was hard making all the ends meet, whilst also being social, going away on weekend trips etc. it is manageable, it was just a lot

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i had first year, second year and third year classes

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: way more online, SO much online stuff to do actually. their version of Absalon/ Canvas is used so much, and youve got to keep up during the semester, because they have midterm exams in week 5, and if you dont pass, theres a high risk of your points cumulatively not making you pass your courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
mental health, psychology and the criminal justice system (really nice and interesting small course)
cognitive psychology (really heavy course)
cognitive neuropsychology (really good course)
positive psychology (sounds easy, is SO much work)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
cognitive neuropsych was definitely one of my favorites - it was really nuanced, and was the course that closest matched the way we get taught, and the mindset brought to the courses at KU. it felt like something i could actually use later in life. 
Mental health, psychology and the criminal justice system was a really good look into the less nice things about australian culture, and specifically the issues that are present in modern day Queensland. the teacher James Ogilvie is one of the best teachers ive had at any university, and he has worked with mental health cases in prisons, institutions, juvys, and with aboriginal and torres straight islanders.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: alcohol was really really expensive - so good on ya if you can party without having a beer first. costwise, australia is just really expensive, so yeah, wasnt reallt surprised by how expensive it all was

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the university student guild provided free groceries every monday and thursday at 2pm - all the basics like greens, beans, pasta, bread. that really helped out my economy. Didnt eat out much, mostly at home because it was SO expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So nice! there were so many opportunities to do stuff - the swimming pool for training, the gym, the free tennis courts. also, the boardriders surf club was pretty active! dont bother signing up for any of the clubs honestly. they didnt do a lot, most clubs made you pay to get in and then no events happened ://

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all sorts! free dinner every tuesday, we did a paint n sip, a musem trip to HOTA, surf club trips, parties, and the O-week was of course also filled with activities. My friend played on the rugby team, another was on the cheerleader team, and there were a lot of options to actually get involved.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: surfing! hiking! just go outside and enjoy the beautiful place. the burleigh beach walk is amazing, the springbrook and tambourine mountains are filled with waterfalls you can swim in and hikes and glowworm caves. there is so much cool stuff to do outside on the coast. Uh! also go to coombabah to see real koalas living in the wild - please dont just go to currumbin wildlife sanctuary - the koalas  look so sad in there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: please please please go to byron bay and broken heads for at least a weekend trip! also go to fraser island, and from the beginning of the semester try to find a group of friends to go on a semester break roadtrip with - driving up to whitsundays, taking a 1 or 2 day cruise and driving back down, whilst also doing fraser island is the coolest thing ever. the weeks go by so fast, and by the semester break, everyone already have their small groups and their plans - going to fraser and great keppel islands and whitsundays and byron is well worth the money! also depending on you schedule, you might have a lot of days off like me - when youre not studying, these can be put into prolonging weekend trips

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: pretty easy - the aussies are nice, well tempered and everything is in english everywhere. the hardest thing to adjust to was walking on the left.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: talk to the people in your classes - you might feel annoying, but theyre actually quite curious, and love to make friends - in general it seems that a lot of aussies know people before they start uni, so they never go to O-week orientation etc. youve gotta catch them in their classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: i was kinda baffled by the fact that the aussies go barefoot anywhere -no shoes in a mall is crazy. but! then i tried it and cant lie, theyre kinda right

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: how easygoing and outdoorsy people are. its more about watching sunset at burleigh hill with your friends, getting up early to surf, going on a roadtrip or hanging out in front of the tele than about glamour and going out. aussies have a strong tall poppy syndrome - jantelov if you must - they dont care who you are, as long as youre nice, and theyll give it to ya straight.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- please please go to O-week! even if it seems lame you make friends forever
- find someone with a car to be your best friend! its SO helpful and will make your experience so much better - heck, if you have the money, buy a car! they range between 7-10.000 AUD depending on the car and how shitty it is
- watch all the sunrises you can! i was skeptical at first, but waking up with the sunrise is amazing. i will carry those mornings by the water, swimming in the sunrise with me for the rest of my life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
theres an on campus doctor - best thing in the world. they are so nice, and with the OSHC, they just batch bill the insurance, so you never pay out of pocket. 
also! speaking of OSHC, buy it yourself through Allianz (the one griffith wants you to get anyway) and send them proof. i purchased my own for 200 AUD, my friend bought hers through uni, where it cost 440 AUD.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: all the friends ive made, and the discovery that saying yes to something new is scary, but noones gonna laugh at me, and everything is gonna be fine.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: balancing keeping in contact with the people at home, and still not alienating myself from my exchange experience. I ended up almost not writing home, because i was so immersed in what was happening in the now, at the gold coast. it was a blessing to put down the phone and just be with the people i was with, but at te same time, it meant that my relationships to the people at home suffered a bit. i wouldnt change anything, but it was a struggle

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: gold coast was the perfect place to go for nature, surfing and that aussie feel - i think this exchange is the best thing ive done in my adult life, and i will honestly be forever grateful for it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
